title: Why some languages make data immutable by default, and what it costs
summary: Clojure, OCaml, Erlang and Rust make immutability the default for reasons of concurrency and reasoning, then pay for it in allocation, asymptotic behaviour and escape hatches such as transients and mutable fields.
